In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no autotransfusion device or leukocyte depleter is capable of completely removing HEP G2 carcinoma cells from blood.
no autotransfusion device is better than any other.
the use of LDF in combination with autotransfusion does not remove all hepatocarcina cells from autotranfusion products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of leukocyte depleters is a viable technique for reducing the number of hepatocarcina cells in autotransfused blood, but the use of autotranfusion devices alone does not appear to be effective.
autotransfusion combined with LDF can remove HEP G2 from expired erythrocytes, but the technique must be optimized for each autotransfusion device.
a combination of autotransfusions devices and leukocyte filters can be used for the treatment of anemia, but should not be utilized for the removal of cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
autotransfusion of blood containing HEP G2 cancer cells is not feasible, regardless of the technique utilized.
autotransfusion with the BRAT2 and STAT-P devices is more effective in removing hepatocarcinomas cells than the CATS device.
autotransfusion of cancerous patients is possible, but requires the use of LDF to remove cancer cells from the blood.
